/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 01 October 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3140 (27)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5010 (82)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2379 (-5)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1794 (-3)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1008 (-4)
CAPESIZE
The BCI 182 5TC gained $741 today to close at $45,435, with much of the support coming from the transpacific round voyage, where the C10 route surged $2,677 to $37,041. After a burst of fixing activity yesterday with both operators and miners active in the West Australia to China market, activity slowed considerably today after China officially entered its Golden Week holiday period. Early indications saw bids emerge slightly above the last concluded levels, although the majority of remaining cargoes carried laycans outside the index assessment window. It was only shortly before the publishing that fresh market evidence surfaced with Norden reportedly fixing the Lady Gwendoline (210,925 2022) for 190,000/10 Port Hedland to Qingdao 20/21 October at $14.50. The fixture offered some support to sentiment, although overall trading remained subdued. Elsewhere, movement was limited. The Brazil market lacked fresh momentum, while the North Atlantic remained relatively quiet, with little new enquiry reported.
PANAMAX
Market sources today reported a slightly slower tone in the Atlantic, with activity easing compared to the levels seen earlier in the week. Sentiment remains generally positive, however, with market fundamentals viewed as largely balanced, this has so far limited any significant movement in rates. Fronthaul sentiment is described as more divided, with brokers highlighting continued grain and mineral demand, although bid and offer spreads remain relatively wide as both Owners and Charterers appear hesitant to commit while awaiting clearer direction in the market. The Aeolian Victory (82,152 2010) passing Madagascar prompt was reported to have fixed an EC South America trans-Atlantic grains trip with Bunge at $35,500. Elsewhere, the Astarte (81,640 2013) Rio Grande 23 October was said to have fixed a similar grains trip basis redelivery passing Gibraltar at $31,000, although market sources differed on the identity of the Charterer. The Pacific is following a similarly balanced tone, with market fundamentals viewed as being fairly evenly matched. Demand from Australia and the North Pacific remains the primary source of activity and is helping to support current rate levels. Available tonnage is also said to be tightening, and with activity reduced by the ongoing national holidays, this is further contributing to a relatively balanced supply and demand dynamic across the basin. The P5TC dropped by $51 to settle at $21,407.
SUPRAMAX
Despite a slow day as the Golden Week holiday started, rates in the Pacific are unaffected so far, with levels maintained around last done and period interest still evident. The Atlantic is far harder to call, especially North America which has seen rates yo-yo this week, with fronthaul rates coming under pressure today. The FJ Viola (61,174 2020) Jacksonville 5 October was said to be on subjects basis delivery SW Pass for a trip Iskenderun with petcoke at $34,000, although another source suggested the rate was $33,000, with Bulk Trading. In the south rates are more stable with limited tonnage available, but with Owners now willing to ballast from the Mediterranean rather than fix local business, this has capped any gains. The Continent remains very firm, although levels no longer appear to be rising, as Charterers push back against Owners offers. The 11TC average made a negative return today, down $33 to finish at $22,681.
HANDYSIZE
The market delivered a mixed performance today, with sentiment largely shaped by positional factors. The BHSI closed at 1,008, while the 7TC average fell by $63 to settle at $18,147. Across the basin, the Continent and Mediterranean maintained their momentum, with fixtures concluded at higher levels. The Cycladic Spire (32,976 2013) open Casablanca early October was fixed for a trip via Cartagena, Spain to Colombia at $15,000 and the Koszalin (37,884 2012) open Volos 7/8 Oct was placed on subjects for Egypt to EC South Atlantic at $11.000, although further details were not disclosed. The US Gulf and South Atlantic slowed slightly, with overall sentiment appearing weak. The Manta Bingul (40,522 2013) open Douala 28 September–2 October was fixed basis delivery Recalada trip to Southeast Asia in the very high $20,000s, although further details were not disclosed. In addition, a 31,000-dwt was heard fixed from Recalada for a coastal trip to Belém in the low $20,000s by Lauritzen, while a 28,000-dwt was fixed for a trip with delivery Dakar via the Plate to the UK at $12,000, although further details were lacking. Meanwhile, the Pacific market moved at a slightly slower pace, with Chinese holidays limiting overall activity. Period enquiry remained present, with the Remy Enterprise (34,529 2019) open Zhoushan reported fixed for a short period at $16,000, although further details were lacking.

Market Fundamentals
HRB Steel Prices
In the two weeks to 30 September, the US hot rolled band (HRB) steel price extended its gains, up $8/t to more than a four-year high of $1,293/t, World Steel Dynamics data show. In contrast, both the Chinese domestic and the Western European HRB steel prices dipped $4/t and $3/t to a respective $424/t and $842/t.
Russian Gain Export Forecast Cut Amid Black Sea Disruptions
Russia’s MY 2026/27 total grain export forecast was downgraded by 4.7 Mt from the prior month to 44.7 Mt, Reuters reports based on agricultural consultancy Sovecon’s estimates. The reduction was entirely attributed to an equivalent decline in wheat exports, which are now forecast at 36.7 Mt for 2026/27. The company ascribed the revision to continued disruptions to Southern Russian port operations as tit-for-tat attacks on vessels and ports in the Black Sea persist, with 90% of Russian seaborne grain transiting via the Black Sea in the prior season.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape was volatile, with a strong morning giving way to a sharp afternoon reversal. Oct firmed from around 40,500–40,750 to 42,000 before falling back sharply, with heavy late volume around 40,000–40,100. Nov reached 43,000 in the morning before retreating toward 41,000 late. Dec traded up to 42,250 before easing back toward 41,000. Q4 26 strengthened from 41,500 to 42,250 before dropping to 40,500–40,850 late.
